thread:
Alex (Finance): Heads-up — accounting flagged ~140 small credit memos applied overnight. NetSuite shows a flurry around 02:45-03:10 UTC. Not huge $ amounts but enough to trigger reconciliation alerts. Anyone know what's up?

billing-bot: nightly-usage-agg finished: job_id=nj-20240613-01, processed=92,412 accounts, warnings=7, errors=1

Jordan (Accounting): Yep, I see them. Many reference the same Stripe invoice id but different memo ids. Looks like duplicates for customers who were part of the "summer-pricing-experiment" cohort.

Priya (Billing): I pulled the Stripe event log — we have multiple invoice.updates for the same invoice with small negative line items around 02:46. Some of those updates were followed by NetSuite pushes that returned 429 and then retried.

Leo (Engineering): NetSuite connector retries are synchronous and do exponential backoff but we don't surface an idempotency key on retry attempts. If the first push made a credit memo before NS returned 429, the retry creates a second memo.

Sam (SRE): Confirmed 429 spikes in the outbound gateway at 02:47 due to a NetSuite API rate limit window. Gateway started retrying automatically. Logs: `ns-gateway status 429 count=37 window=60s`.

Alex (Finance): So it's a race between price-experiment backfills + NetSuite throttling causing duplicate memos on retries. Can we stop outbound to NetSuite for the affected invoice range until we dedupe?

Priya (Billing): I'll pause the NetSuite queue for billing-org for invoices created 2024-06-12..2024-06-13. Putting a hold now.

billing-bot: outbound-queue paused: target=netSuite, scope=org:billing, by=priya at 1718310120

Leo (Engineering): Plan proposal: 1) Add idempotency_token header to every NetSuite push using `ns_idempotency:{source}:{event_id}` 2) Change retry logic to include that token so retries won't create duplicates 3) Add a reconciliation pass to collapse memos produced between 02:40-03:20 and generate a CSV for accounting.

Jordan (Accounting): CSV needs customer tier, invoice id, original memo ids, amounts, and suggested action (reverse/merge). Also include a count of enterprise customers touched.

Sam (SRE): I can throttle the connector to 5r/s while we roll the change. Also recommend a small circuit-breaker: if 429 rate > 10/min, pause outbound automatically.

Leo (Engineering): I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/netSuite-connector/pull/129 — adds idempotency header + retry propagation + circuit-breaker. Will run unit tests and deploy to staging.

Alex (Finance): Do we need approval from Accounting for reconciliation script to mark NetSuite memos as "merged"? We prefer manual review for enterprise tier.

Jordan (Accounting): Yes, manual signoff for enterprise only. For non-enterprise we can auto-merge per rules in the CSV. I'll review the staging CSV first.

Priya (Billing): FYI the pricing experiment backfill emitted these delta payloads (example):
```
{ "account": "acct_xyz", "experiment": "summer-pricing-2024", "delta_cents": -200, "backfill_id": "bf-778" }
```
Backfill job id bf-778 had 1,200 accounts and was set to `emit_reconciler_events=true`. The reconciler generated invoice_update events which hit the connector.

Sam (SRE): Staging deploy queued at 1718310300. I'll gradually push to prod behind the throttle once staging looks clean.

billing-bot: staging-deploy started: deploy_id=deploy-1718310320, component=netSuite-connector

Leo (Engineering): Staging results: connector included idempotency header, retries returned 200 for repeated payloads (no duplicate memos). Recon dry-run collapsed 136 duplicate candidates into 28 suggested merges.

Priya (Billing): Great. Jordan — I'll generate the CSV from staging dry-run and DM you.

Jordan (Accounting): Got it. Quick question — for merged memos, do we create a single correcting memo or void the duplicates and issue a net adjustment? Prefer void+reissue so audit trail is clear.

Alex (Finance): Void + reissue sounds good. Ensure the recon script outputs the exact NS commands for accounting to run (or we can run via admin with approval).

Sam (SRE): Rolling to prod now with throttling and circuit-breaker enabled. Will monitor 429s and pause if spike > threshold.

billing-bot: prod-deploy finished: deploy_id=deploy-1718310445, component=netSuite-connector, status=success

Leo (Engineering): Recon job run on prod window 2024-06-12T02:30..2024-06-13T03:30 produced CSV: `duplicate-memos-1718310500.csv` (s3://redwood-billing/recon/). CSV includes tiers and enterprise flags.

Jordan (Accounting): Reviewing CSV now. Found 12 enterprise customers affected — will escalate to account teams before any NetSuite changes. For the rest, I approve automated void+reissue after a 1-hour waiting period for any late arrivals.

Priya (Billing): I've re-enabled outbound for scoped invoices after Jordan approval for non-enterprise. Enterprise invoices remain paused.

billing-bot: outbound-queue resumed: target=netSuite, scope=org:billing:non-enterprise by priya at 1718310565

Alex (Finance): Thanks everyone. Action items: Leo to merge PR + post-deploy runbook update; Sam to add automatic pause on 429 spike; Jordan to run approved CSV jobs and notify account teams for enterprise; Priya to monitor AR alerts for the next 48h.

Leo (Engineering): Will open follow-up ticket to backfill idempotency for older connectors and add unit test for retry behavior.

Sam (SRE): Monitoring set up, alert if duplicate memo rate > 0.1% of invoices in a 1h window.

Alex (Finance): Closing thread for now. Please add a short postmortem note in the billing-runbook referencing this incident and the new circuit-breaker + idempotency header change.
